brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut toward the ₹0.65–0.80/pc band the market allows at higher volume, and lock in a robust second source from the five proven alternates.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% reduction on rigid plastic packaging, targeting the lower end of the market band.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc for items like the 28 mm cap (currently asked at ₹0.85–0.95/pc in the market)
priceAsk.basis: The market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with the verdict 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'. We spend ₹44.37 L annually — enough volume to justify moving down that band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 Days After Receipt terms; no change needed.

brief.financialLeverage: Rachana Plastics publishes no financials, so we cannot see their revenue, profit, or how tight their cash is. That means we build our plan on our own spend data, the market pricing, and lining up a second source. Our ₹44.37 L annual spend is meaningful for a private converter, giving us room to ask — but without their numbers we lean harder on the five proven alternates (three listed firms, two strong private players) to show we have credible options and won't be locked in.

evidence.point: Market pricing shows room to move lower at higher volume or looser specs
evidence.figure: 28 mm induction-wad PP cap ask band ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'

evidence.point: Our annual spend with them is substantial for a packaging converter
HDPE resin import price provides a raw-material benchmark
We pay them 30 Days After Receipt, a standard term
Rachana's financials are not public, so we cannot assess their cash position or health

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, does pharma bottles/caps/preforms; health score B (65/100), revenue ₹2569.83 Cr — the strongest second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, and pharma packaging; described as strong and profitable — a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed firm with broad moulded and blow-moulded packaging capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Rachana's financials are not public, so we fly blind on their cash position — if they hit trouble, supply continuity is at risk.
We have no internal price benchmark (no bestPriceWePay) for rigid plastic packaging, so the market ask is our only anchor — validate it with an RFQ to one alternate before the meeting.
Pushing too hard without a qualified second source in hand may leave us scrambling if Rachana walks; get at least one alternate priced and audited first.
The market backups are leads (recyclers and manufacturers) — none are qualified yet, so do not rely on them as live options until we verify capacity and pricing.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and with our ₹44.37 L annual spend we'd like to discuss how we can both benefit from moving toward the ₹0.65–0.80 price band the market supports at higher volume.
